info.name: ZoikoTax API (v1)
info.description:
**Generated from `contracts/openapi/ztax.v1.yaml` — do not edit.**

Run `npm run postman` in `contracts/` after changing the contract or the overlay. A hand edit fails CI (ADR-0010 §2.1): a hand-maintained collection is a second, kinder statement of what the API is.

Contract digest: `sha256:e5cfae3c5dad428ce8828f0d7e4919dc5888f0a74c118be81ae1437b1920072e`

Import and run; there is no environment to select. `baseUrl` defaults to the local cell and every other value rides along as a collection variable.

## Before you run it

Bring the stack up (`docker compose up --build`), which bootstraps the `acme` tenant and its administrator. Then run the whole collection: `02 · Sign in` opens the session everything below depends on.

Folders `05`, `07` and `90` are the ones worth reading. Each request there sends something a well-behaved client would never send, and each asserts a control from the ADRs against an endpoint that exists today.

Folders `06` and `07` exercise the determination surface and are skipped unless `runDetermination` is `true`: they need a cell with a content bundle and a session holding `OPERATOR`, which the local stack's bootstrap administrator does not have. `98 · Destructive` is skipped unless `runDestructive` is `true`.

item.name: 00 · Health — served, and deliberately not in the contract
item.description:
An orchestrator calls these; no SDK does. They carry no session, their bodies are plain text, and declaring them in the contract would generate client methods nobody should call and make a liveness probe a compatibility commitment (ADR-0010 §2.6).

They are added by the generator rather than derived from the contract, and `contract_test.go` keeps the same exception register on the server side.

Open a session

Exchanges a tenant slug, an email address and a password for an opaque

The response carries **no token**. The session identifier is in a

item.name: 04 · Administration
item.description:
Runs in order: list, create, grant, disable, then read the sessions and the audit trail, then undo. `createUser` captures the new user's id into `userId`, so the requests after it act on something that exists.

Then webhooks: `createWebhook` subscribes an endpoint and captures `webhookId`; the secret is shown once and asserted to be in the Standard Webhooks form. A fresh run has delivered nothing, so the delivery read and replay answer `404` for the example delivery id, and the run ends by pausing the webhook. The local stack sets `ZTAX_WEBHOOK_KEY_REF`; a cell without one answers `503`.

Last, period seals: `sealPeriod` seals the example day and captures `sealId`, then the seal is read with its signed payload and verified. A cell with no seal keyring answers `503`, one with a keyring and no signer refuses the seal with `503`, and a period sealed already answers `409`.

Then retention: `recordRetentionPolicy` records the next version of the example policy, so each run adds one. `placeLegalHold` places a hold on the example line and captures `holdId`; the hold is read, its scope widened and then released, which is final — the next run places a new one. Each hold read is written to the audit trail as privileged evidence access. `getDecisionRetention` asks for the verdict on `{{decisionId}}`, which this folder has not made, so it answers `404`.

Last, legal authorization: the matrix the cell loaded is read — the local stack mounts the development one, a draft — then `grantAuthorization` records a filing mandate for the tenant's default legal entity and captures `authorizationId`. `checkAuthorization` asks whether September may be filed with the authority under it, and `revokeAuthorization` revokes it, after which the same check would be blocked. Then payee master data: `createBeneficiary` records an authority's payee details and captures `beneficiaryId`; the same administrator verifying them is refused with `MAKER_CHECKER` (ZTAX-REM-REQ-0014), and the version is suspended. Then support: `openSupportCase` opens a LEGAL case and captures `caseId`; the queue and the case are read, and `actOnSupportCase` verifies the requester, which moves the case to `VERIFIED` as one more event in its history. Then entitlements: `createEntitlement` records a UK filing right from today, submitted for review, and captures `entitlementId`; the same administrator approving it is refused with `MAKER_CHECKER` (Doc 18 W07), so it stays `PENDING`. `proposeSubscriptionPlan` proposes a plan and captures `planId`, and its proposer approving it is refused the same way. `getUsage` counts the month from the cell's own records, exact integers with a basis digest each, and `getUsageBasis` lists the rows one meter counted. Then a migration: `createMigrationProgram` creates a program for 2025 and captures `migrationProgramId`; a snapshot of two historical results is registered, a mapping that names only one of their legacy codes is recorded, and `executeMigrationRun` converts the snapshot AS_KNOWN — one record converts, the other raises an `UNMAPPED_CODE` exception, captured into `migrationExceptionId`, and the monetary reconciliation does not pass. The exception is accepted as a known residual and the cutover moves to `PRECHECK`.

Last, the dashboard: `getDashboard` reads the Tax Command Center for the current month. It needs `OPERATOR`, `ANALYST` or `AUDITOR`; the local stack grants its bootstrap administrator `ANALYST` for exactly this, and a cell that does not answers `403`.

item.name: POST /v1/seals — Seal a period's decisions

request.description:
Seal a period's decisions

`ADMIN` only. Signs a statement that the decisions recorded in
`[periodStart, periodEnd)` were exactly these, with exactly these
results: an RFC 6962 Merkle root over one leaf per decision, signed
with the evidence-seal key together with the tenant, cell and period,
so the signature cannot be lifted onto anything else (ADR-0011 §2.5).

A period may be sealed only after it has settled — five minutes past
its end — so a decision whose transaction was still committing is not
left out. Periods never overlap: a decision is vouched for by one seal
or none. A cell with no seal signer refuses with `503`; it can still
verify seals and prove inclusion.

A seal is integrity evidence, not a legal finality marker: it says the
record has not changed, not that the figures in it were right.

item.name: POST /v1/support/cases/{caseId}/actions — Take one action on a support case

request.description:
Take one action on a support case

`ADMIN`, `OPERATOR` or `ANALYST`, signed in as themselves.

Every action appends one event to the case's single audited history;
nothing is edited. `VERIFY` moves `NEW` to `VERIFIED`. `TRIAGE`
classifies the case and moves it to `TRIAGED`, or to
`TRIAGE_INCOMPLETE` with the facts requested when the contract, the
impacted period or the seller is missing (SUP-02). `START_REVIEW` and
`ESCALATE` move it to `IN_REVIEW`; `RESPOND` records the customer
response, `RESOLVE` follows it, and `CLOSE` ends the case.
`REOPEN` takes a resolved or closed case back to `IN_REVIEW`, linked to
the event it reverses (SUP-07). `ASSIGN`, `REQUEST_EVIDENCE`,
`ADD_EVIDENCE`, `SIGN_OFF`, `NOTE` and `REQUEST_LEGAL_HOLD` change no
status; a legal hold request is recorded for an administrator, and
places no hold.

`CLOSE` needs a customer response since the last reopening, or
`409 STATE_TRANSITION_INVALID` (SUP-14). A case that is, or was ever,
`LEGAL` or `TAX_SPECIALIST` also needs a sign-off since the last
reopening by someone other than its opener, or `409 SIGN_OFF_REQUIRED`;
the opener's own sign-off is `403 SEGREGATION_OF_DUTIES` (T18-18).

Neither clock is reset: a raised severity can bring the SLA due time
earlier, measured from opening, and a statutory deadline once recorded
is never changed by support (SUP-07). An action the status does not
allow is `409 STATE_TRANSITION_INVALID`.

with a different body is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE`; a key whose first
request is still running is `409 REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS` with
`Retry-After`. Neither executes. Bodies are compared in canonical form,
so member order and whitespace do not matter and a decimal's scale
does — `"45.00"` and `"45.0"` are different requests.

A validation failure is recorded against the key and replayed on
retry, because the same request fails the same way. A transient
failure (`503`) is not: the key is released and a retry is a genuine
new attempt.

`supersedes` corrects an earlier decision for the same `businessKey`.
It must name the current version; a decision is never edited, and a
correction is a new decision linked to the old (ADR-0003).

When the active content binds its accumulators to the cell (a
bundle fiscal profile), the cell reads them under lock before
evaluating, records this decision's contribution, and posts the
decision to the Tax Control Subledger, all in this request's
transaction. A request that supplies a value for a bound accumulator
is refused with `400 INVALID_VALUE`: the store is the source
(ZTAX-DET-REQ-0002). `accumulators` remains for content that reads a
value the cell does not hold.

Before A4 every decision is `ADVISORY` and `authoritative: false`.

A `document` commit records the document, every line's situs decision
and components, and the totals in the envelope and result, so a replay
reproduces it exactly under the content that made it. A decision whose
document is not `RESOLVED` is recorded and emits nothing: it posts no

A reversal names the source event it reverses in `reverses` and carries
negative bases; it is a contribution of its own, never an edit, and an
original is reversed at most once (`409 ALREADY_EXISTS`) and by no more
than it contributed (UAT-OBL-027). A reversal whose original is not yet
recorded is accepted, and its period is `DATA_INCOMPLETE` until the

item.name: POST /v1/workpapers/{workpaperId}/actions — Freeze, review, approve, or record an adjustment, rate or resolution

request.description:
Freeze, review, approve, or record an adjustment, rate or resolution

`OPERATOR` or `ANALYST`, signed in as themselves; `APPROVE`,
`DECIDE_ADJUSTMENT` and `DECIDE_RESOLUTION` need `ANALYST`.

One act, named by `action`, appended to the workpaper's history:

- `DOCUMENT_FX_RATE` documents the rate and conversion basis for one
  source currency (`fx`). A source currency without one is a
  `CURRENCY_MISMATCH` exception until it is documented and rebuilt.
- `PROPOSE_ADJUSTMENT` records a permitted allowance or an audited
  adjustment in the reporting currency, with its `evidence`. One at or
  above the materiality threshold waits for a second person:
  `DECIDE_ADJUSTMENT` by someone other than the proposer
  (`403 SEGREGATION_OF_DUTIES`).
- `PROPOSE_RESOLUTION` explains one resolvable exception of the latest
  build, with its `evidence` and the exception's `fingerprint`;
  `DECIDE_RESOLUTION` confirms or rejects it, by someone else.
- `FREEZE` locks the latest build for review. Refused with
  `403 WORKPAPER_NOT_READY` while any exception is unresolved, a decision
  is pending, or the basis changed since the build — material data
  absent never reaches `READY_FOR_REVIEW`.
- `RETURN_TO_DRAFT` unlocks a frozen workpaper, with the reason.
- `APPROVE` approves the frozen `buildVersion`. The approver neither froze
  it nor ran it.
- `CHANGE_BASIS` records a new `contentRelease`; it revokes an approval
  and unlocks a frozen workpaper.

Writes to a frozen workpaper's inputs are `409 WORKPAPER_SNAPSHOT_LOCKED`.
`expectedSeq`, when given, is the number of events the caller read; a
workpaper that has moved since is `409 WORKPAPER_STALE`.

Records a registration a legal entity holds or is applying for: its

supporting documents by digest (hashed in the browser; nothing is
uploaded). It is kept as a `DRAFT`, or `SUBMITTED` with `submit: true`

official acceptance (Doc 17 ER-014). The legal entity defaults to the
tenant's default entity.

is edited.

the registration already recorded with `200`; the same key with a
different request is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE`.

request.description:
Authorise and dispatch a sealed batch

`OPERATOR` or `ANALYST`, signed in as themselves, and not the person who
prepared the batch (`403 MAKER_CHECKER`).

The checker names the batch digest they reviewed (`409
ERP_BATCH_DIGEST_MISMATCH` when it is not the batch's). The dispatch is
one attempt, recorded with a `com.zoikotax.gl.export-dispatched` event
through the transactional outbox in the same transaction; a connector
subscribed to it sends the batch under its `externalRef`, which every
attempt shares, so the ERP posts one GL journal however many attempts
there are. `TRANSMITTED` means committed for transmission — not
received, and not posted.

**Idempotent on the batch.** A batch already transmitted, acknowledged
or posted is returned as it is with `200` and no new attempt
(QA-LED-069). A batch sealed under a superseded mapping version is
refused (`409 ERP_MAPPING_CHANGED`, QA-LED-068). A batch whose outcome
is unknown is sent again only after a status query recorded that the
ERP holds nothing under its reference (`409 ERP_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`). A
rejected or withdrawn batch is never sent.

item.name: POST /v1/erp-bridges/{bridgeId}/exports/{batchId}/responses — Record what the ERP answered about an attempt

request.description:
Record what the ERP answered about an attempt

`OPERATOR` or `ANALYST`, signed in as themselves.

ZoikoTax does not invent the ERP's answer: a person records it here with
the ERP's references as evidence. `ACKNOWLEDGED` is a transport receipt
and names the ERP's `remoteCorrelation`; `POSTED` names the ERP's posted
journal (`erpReference`) and is the only answer a GL reconciliation
counts. `REJECTED` says why, opens a correction task and holds the
period's GL reconciliation. `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` says why nobody knows.

found nothing under the batch's reference — the only thing that lets a
batch of unknown outcome be sent again.

again records nothing and answers `200`. An answer that does not apply
to the batch's state is `409 STATE_TRANSITION_INVALID`.

`"amount": 45.0` must be rejected, never coerced. A 2xx here is a Critical finding rather than a test failure: RFC 8785 serializes JSON numbers through IEEE 754 doubles (ADR-0011 §1.1), so an amount that is ever a JSON number has lost precision before canonicalization sees it — and the loss is invisible, because 45.0 survives and 0.1 does not.

item.name: POST /v1/auth/password-reset — Email a password-reset link

request.description:
Email a password-reset link

Emails a one-time link that sets a new password to the account at this
tenant and address, if there is one. An invited user who never set a
password is sent a fresh invitation instead; a disabled account is sent
nothing.

**The answer is always 202**, whether or not the account exists: which
accounts exist is not the caller's to learn. The message is sent off the
request path for the same reason, so its round trip to the mail server
does not time the answer. A reset link expires after an hour and works
once, and issuing one spends every earlier one.

Answers 503 when the cell sends no mail, and 429 when one client or one
address asks too often.
